## Blocker cluster: Cluster-1-Auth

**Root cause:** Session cache corruption in the Auth service (SharedCompFailure archetype).

| Squad | Blocker count | Active days (2026) | Waiting Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auth (root) | 3 | Jul 15–17 | "Session cache corruption in Auth service; fix in progress" |
| Checkout (cascade) | 3 | Jul 16–18 | "Waiting on Login service (SQ-A)" |
| Payments (cascade) | 3 | Jul 16–18 | "Waiting on Login service (SQ-A)" |

**Cascade timing:** Auth is blocked for 3 days (days 1–3 of week 3); Checkout and Payments each start 1 day after Auth (cascade lag) and clear 1 day after Auth resolves (propagation lag) — visible directly in the `Created` timestamps above. No blockers occur outside week 3 (the nominal "weeks 3–5" cluster window from `ARCHITECTURE.md` is where the cluster is described, but Task 1.3's actual injected activity is entirely within week 3).

## Blocker density

| Scope | Value | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Global (all 12 sprints) | 1.4% | ~1–2% (single-cluster MVP; full percolation is Sprint 3's 3-cluster/8-squad scope) |
| Week 3 only (cluster's actual window) | 28.1% | 20–30% |

Density is deliberately not uniform: it's a small, visible spike concentrated in the exact days the Auth cluster is active, not a diffuse pattern across the dataset. See `GitHub Issue #2` for how this two-tier (window vs. global) density target was reconciled with the original single global 20–30% figure, which was mathematically unreachable at this cluster's size.

## What a viewer should see when loading this into a pivot/viz tool

1. Filter `v1_auth_cluster_high_density.csv` to `Status = Waiting` — all 9 rows fall in a tight 4-day window (Jul 15–18, 2026), one visible cluster.
2. Group by `Assignee` and `Created` date — Auth's blocker appears first (Jul 15), Checkout/Payments follow exactly one day later (Jul 16) and clear one day after Auth resolves.
3. Every `Waiting` row's `Waiting Reason` references Auth or "Login service" — no unrelated or orphaned blockers.
4. Cross-reference `v1_auth_cluster_test_logs.csv`'s `Flaky = true` rows against `Sprint` — flaky tests concentrate in Sprint 2 (which contains week 3), not spread evenly across all 12 sprints.

## Known limitations (Sprint 1 scope)

- Only 3 of the eventual 8 squads are modeled (Sprint 2 adds Core Banking/Savings; Sprint 3 completes the topology).
- Only 1 of the eventual 3 blocker clusters is injected (DataPlatform and Checkout-instability clusters are Sprint 2/3).
- Global blocker density (~1–2%) will not, by itself, visually demonstrate a percolation-threshold "flow stall" — that requires Sprint 3's full topology. Sprint 1's purpose is narrower: prove the cluster's cascade timing and density are correctly modeled and visible in isolation, per `BACKLOG.md`'s stated goal ("Prove the percolation hypothesis works at the smallest scale").
